source_refs.note: Topic 19.8 with Quick Check 19.6, answered (PDF 50-51); the mechanisms are redrawn. The propagation steps of methane chlorination are given for the stages the book names. The HBr addition is shown with its carbocation step. Answers need review.

blocks.text: A mechanism is the pathway a reaction follows, showing the bonds that break and form as the substrate turns into the product. Mechanisms are of two main types, depending on the reagent: free-radical and ionic (polar).

This involves homolysis, producing free radicals that attack the substrate. An example is the chlorination of methane in diffused sunlight, which overall can go as far as CH4 + 4Cl2 -> CCl4 + 4HCl. The reaction has three stages: initiation, in which light splits Cl2 into two Cl. radicals; propagation, in which radicals react to form products and more radicals (Cl. + CH4 -> HCl + .CH3, then .CH3 + Cl2 -> CH3Cl + Cl.); and termination, in which two radicals combine and the chain stops.

items: Nucleophilic substitution: a nucleophile attacks a saturated, electrophilic carbon and replaces another group, the leaving group, e.g. OH- + CH3Br -> CH3OH + Br- through a transition state.

Nucleophilic addition: a nucleophile attacks the electrophilic carbon of a carbonyl compound, giving an addition product, e.g. CN- adds to ethanal and the anion takes H+ from HCN, giving 2-hydroxypropanenitrile.
Electrophilic addition: an electrophile attacks an electron-rich site such as a C=C or C triple bond, e.g. HBr adds to ethene giving bromoethane.
Elimination: two atoms or groups are removed from neighbouring carbon atoms, forming a double or triple bond, e.g. OH- removes H from bromoethane as Br- leaves, giving ethene.

blocks.alt: H-O- (nucleophile, with a lone pair) attacks the carbon of bromomethane (H on a dashed bond, H on a wedge, H on a plain bond; C +delta, Br -delta); a curved arrow goes from O to C and another from the C-Br bond to Br. This gives a bracketed transition state with charge (-): HO, C and Br joined by dashed lines, three H on C, HO and Br -delta, C +delta. It then gives methanol, H-O-C with three H, plus Br- (leaving group).
blocks.caption: Nucleophilic substitution: hydroxide ion and bromomethane give methanol through a transition state (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure).

blocks.alt: N triple-bond C- with a lone pair attacks the +delta carbon of ethanal (C=O with O -delta, H3C and H on the carbon); one curved arrow goes from the lone pair to C and another from the C=O bond to O. This gives N-C-C(H)(CH3) with O- carrying lone pairs. With H-CN (+delta H, -delta CN) it gives 2-hydroxy propanenitrile, N-C-C(OH)(CH3)-H, plus CN-.
blocks.caption: Nucleophilic addition: cyanide ion adds to ethanal, giving 2-hydroxypropanenitrile (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure).

blocks.alt: H2C=CH2 (ethene) plus H-Br with H +delta and Br -delta; a curved arrow runs from the C=C double bond to H. The arrow leads to CH3-CH2-Br (bromoethane).
blocks.caption: Electrophilic addition: ethene and hydrogen bromide give bromoethane (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure).

blocks.alt: HO- with a lone pair plus bromoethane, drawn as CH2-CH2-Br with an H above the first carbon; the carbon bonded to Br is +delta and Br -delta. Three curved arrows: from the HO- lone pair to the H, from the C-H bond to the C-C bond, and from the C-Br bond to Br. The products are CH2=CH2 (ethene) + H2O + Br-.
blocks.caption: Elimination: hydroxide ion and bromoethane give ethene, water and bromide ion (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed scheme marks the CH2 bonded to Br as -delta; bromine is more electronegative than carbon, so that carbon is +delta, as drawn above.

items: Describe NH3, Br. (a bromine atom), H2O, NO2+ and Cl(delta+) as electrophile, nucleophile or free radical.
Classify: (i) CH3CH=CH2 + HBr -> CH3CHBrCH3; (ii) CH4 + Br2 -> CH3Br + HBr; (iii) CH3CH2CHClCH3 -> CH3CH2CH=CH2 + HCl.
